note: Curated New England solar / net-metering / REC market / regulatory updates for array operators. Each item is tagged with its state (or "region" for New England-wide, "rec" for REC-market-wide); the page filters to the reader's state. Refreshed by a research agent; verify against the linked source before relying on any figure.

items.title: Eversource files ~$727M CT electric rate case seeking ~18% residential hike
items.summary: The Connecticut Light and Power Company (Eversource) filed its first electric distribution rate review in nearly a decade with PURA, seeking roughly $727 million in added annual revenue and an estimated 18% increase for the typical residential customer, driven largely by 2018–2025 storm costs. If approved, new rates would take effect July 1, 2027; Attorney General William Tong called the request a 'tone-deaf insult.'

items.title: NH enacts HB 1718 creating net-metering credits for solar-charged batteries
items.summary: Gov. Kelly Ayotte signed HB 1718 on July 10, 2026, directing the Department of Energy and PUC to build a framework compensating customers for electricity exported to the grid from batteries charged by renewable generators, clarifying that storage can pair with net-metered solar without affecting system-size limits.

items.title: New Hampshire joins states with plug-in ('balcony') solar law under SB 540
items.summary: SB 540, signed May 28, 2026 and effective July 27, 2026, legalizes portable plug-in solar devices capped at one unit per meter and 1,200 watts, exempting them from interconnection agreements and net-metering rules while requiring UL-type safety certification.

items.title: RI 2026 session recap: solar 'grid access fee' killed, large-solar credits cut
items.summary: Gov. McKee's proposed grid-access fee on net-metering systems of at least 1 MW was eliminated after pushback from developers, unions, and clean-energy advocates; a working-group deal instead lowers virtual-net-metering compensation for large solar. The session ended June 11, 2026, and Solar Cost Reduction Act and balcony-solar bills passed the House but stalled in the Senate.

items.title: Maine DOER holds first public webinar on front-of-the-meter DER successor program
items.summary: Maine's Department of Energy Resources held Public Webinar #1 on June 25, 2026, presenting its approach and timeline for a new front-of-the-meter distributed energy resources program to replace community-solar NEB. The proposed successor program must be submitted to the MPUC by the statutory deadline of September 30, 2026.

items.title: Vermont PUC's 2026 net-metering order cuts solar compensation for a 7th straight year
items.summary: In Case 26-0291-INV the Public Utility Commission's late-May biennial order reduces net-metering adjustors for all new systems by about 2¢/kWh and raises the small-solar siting charge from 4¢ to 5¢/kWh for systems permitted Aug 1, 2026 through Jul 31, 2028. Over 1,000 Vermonters and more than 50 House members had urged the PUC to reject the cuts.

items.title: NH net metering's future stays murky as legislative session closes
items.summary: SB 538, extending net-metering eligibility for municipal group projects already in the interconnection queue, cleared a committee of conference and headed to the governor, while SB 449 (net metering for 1–5 MW commercial/industrial arrays) was voted inexpedient to legislate. Existing net-metering terms still expire in 2040.

items.title: Rhode Island Energy base distribution rate case (Docket 25-45-GE) holds public hearing
items.summary: Rhode Island Energy's application (filed Nov 26, 2025) seeks a two-year rate plan with a first-year base-distribution increase of roughly $65.9M electric and $114.7M gas; Docket 25-33-GE was consolidated into it in April 2026. The PUC held a public comment hearing June 10, 2026, in Warwick.

items.title: Maine PUC holds hearings on CMP's distribution rate proposal
items.summary: Central Maine Power, which serves about 670,000 customers, is seeking a $69 million temporary distribution rate increase in a case expected to run roughly 11 months. Public witness hearings were held June 9 (South Portland) and June 23 (Lewiston).

items.title: Renewable Energy Vermont blasts PUC net-metering cuts in biennial rate update
items.summary: REV's press statement criticizes the PUC's biennial order for raising the small-solar siting charge from 4¢ to 5¢/kWh (effective Aug 1, 2026–Jul 31, 2028) and cutting adjustors, noting net-metering applications for systems under 150 kW fell 24% from 2024 to 2025.

items.title: ISO New England says grid ready for summer; 8,000+ MW of behind-the-meter solar
items.summary: ISO-NE forecasts a normal-weather summer peak of 25,228 MW (26,473 MW under above-average heat) against 28,717 MW of available resources, and reports more than 8,000 MW of behind-the-meter solar expected to cut demand by over 1,700 MW at the peak hour, pushing the daily peak to 5–6 p.m.

items.title: Massachusetts DPU approves SMART 3.0 solar incentive redesign
items.summary: On May 19, 2026 the DPU approved a redesigned SMART incentive that replaces the declining-block structure with rates DOER adjusts annually, plus capacity allocations. Utilities estimate the revised program will cost ratepayers about $4.5 billion over 20 years for projects enrolling in program years 2025 and 2026.

items.title: ISO-NE adds behind-the-meter batteries to its 2026 forecast
items.summary: The 2026 CELT Report for the first time includes behind-the-meter battery storage (sub-1 MW paired with solar), currently about 111 MW region-wide, and projects behind-the-meter PV reaching 5,500 MW by end of 2026 and 7,950 MW by 2035, cutting grid energy use by more than 7,000 GWh this year.

items.title: MA Class I RECs trend toward the $40 ACP as MassCEC auctions 2025-vintage certificates
items.summary: MassCEC's May 14, 2026 REC auction offered 4,629 Vintage 2025 MA Class I RECs and 67 Solar Carve-Out II RECs; Evolution Markets said Class I 2025 REC pricing has been trending toward the $40/MWh Alternative Compliance Payment in a supply-constrained market ahead of the 2025 compliance deadline.

items.title: PURA cuts Eversource and UI rates effective May 1, 2026
items.summary: PURA conditionally approved lower electric rates for Eversource and United Illuminating via their annual Rate Adjustment Mechanisms, effective May 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027 — cutting Eversource residential rates about 4.3¢/kWh (~$30/month) and UI about 4.9¢/kWh (~$34/month), driven mainly by the public-benefits charge turning into a credit tied to Millstone/Seabrook contract savings.

items.title: LD 1777 effectively halts new community solar in Maine
items.summary: Under LD 1777, Maine utilities are barred from accepting new community solar projects and existing 1–5 MW-AC arrays face new monthly charges ($2.80/kW-AC for 1–3 MW-AC, $6/kW-AC for 3–5 MW-AC) effective Jan 1, 2026. Nautilus Solar and Nexamp said they will not develop new Maine community solar, and the industry has sued the MPUC over the fees.

items.title: MA DPU opens net-metering investigation — Docket 25-200
items.summary: The DPU opened Docket 25-200 to examine electric delivery rate design and whether to reduce the value of net-metering credits, comparing Massachusetts crediting to lower-compensation jurisdictions. No changes have been ordered; existing systems are expected to be grandfathered.
